scenes.heading: Index laws review
scenes.say: How would you simplify two x squared y, all to the power of four? It looks scary, but five simple index laws handle it in a few short steps.
scenes.caption: How would you simplify (2x²y)⁴? It looks scary, but five simple index laws handle it in a few short steps.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Crates of 2³ tins on pallets of 2⁴ crates: 2⁷ tins per pallet
scenes.science: Joining groups adds indices; copying a group multiplies them
scenes.breaks: You can't have minus 3 crates, but the laws still work for zero and negative indices.
scenes.say: Picture a warehouse. A crate holds two cubed tins, and a pallet holds two to the four crates. That is two cubed times two to the four, or two to the seven tins. Joining groups adds the indices. Copying a whole group several times, like two to the seven, cubed, multiplies them.
scenes.caption: A crate holds 2³ tins, and a pallet holds 2⁴ crates. That is 2³ × 2⁴ = 2⁷ tins. Joining groups adds the indices. Copying a whole group, like (2⁷)³, multiplies them.

scenes.heading: The index laws
points: Same base only; the base never changes
scenes.say: Here are the laws. Multiplying powers with the same base, add the indices. Dividing, subtract. A power of a power, multiply. And a bracket raised to a power gives that power to every factor inside, numbers included. These only work when the bases match.

scenes.heading: Power of a product
scenes.say: Two x cubed y, all to the fourth. The four goes to everything. Two to the four is sixteen. x cubed to the four is x to the twelve. And y to the four. So sixteen x to the twelve, y to the four. The classic mistake is forgetting to raise the two.
scenes.caption: (2x³y)⁴: the 4 goes to everything. 2⁴ = 16, (x³)⁴ = x¹², and y⁴. So 16x¹²y⁴. The classic mistake is forgetting to raise the 2.

scenes.heading: Dividing terms
scenes.question: Simplify 24m⁸n⁵ ÷ 8m³n.
scenes.say: Simplify twenty-four m to the eight, n to the five, divided by eight m cubed n. Numbers first: twenty-four divided by eight is three. Then m to the eight divided by m cubed is m to the five. n on its own is n to the one, so n to the five divided by n is n to the four. Answer: three m to the five n to the four.
scenes.caption: Simplify 24m⁸n⁵ ÷ 8m³n. 24 ÷ 8 = 3. m⁸ ÷ m³ = m⁵. n is n¹, so n⁵ ÷ n = n⁴. Answer: 3m⁵n⁴.

scenes.heading: Brackets first
scenes.question: Simplify (2p³)⁴ × p² ÷ 4p⁵.
scenes.say: A longer one. Deal with the bracket first: two p cubed, to the four, is sixteen p to the twelve. Times p squared gives sixteen p to the fourteen. Divide by four p to the five: sixteen over four is four, and fourteen take five is nine. Answer: four p to the nine.
scenes.caption: Bracket first: (2p³)⁴ = 16p¹². Times p² gives 16p¹⁴. Divide by 4p⁵: 16 ÷ 4 = 4, and 14 − 5 = 9. Answer: 4p⁹.

points: Bracket: the index goes to every factor
scenes.say: Quick recap. Multiplying powers, add the indices. Dividing, subtract. Power of a power, multiply. A bracket's index goes to every factor, numbers too. And coefficients follow normal arithmetic. Now try the practice questions!
